chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, may God have mercy on him, narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih ibn Sa'd al-Tamimi narrated to us, from his father, he said: Ahmad ibn Hisham narrated to us, he said: Mansur ibn Mujahid narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Badr, from Sawwar ibn Munib, from Wahb, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, blessings of God upon him and his family, said:
Indeed God, blessed and exalted, has an angel named Sakha'il who takes the writs for those who pray at every prayer from the Lord of the Worlds, exalted is His majesty.

When the believers wake at dawn and rise, perform ablution, and pray the Fajr prayer, he brings from God, mighty and majestic, a writ for them, written therein: 'I am God, the Everlasting. My servants and handmaids, I have placed you in My protection and in My safeguarding, and under My care I have made you. By My glory, I will not forsake you, and your sins are forgiven until Dhuhr.'

When the time of Dhuhr comes and they rise, perform ablution, and pray, he brings for them from God, mighty and majestic, the second writ, written therein: 'I am God, the All-Powerful. My servants and handmaids, I have changed your evil deeds into good deeds, and I have forgiven your sins, and I have settled you through My pleasure with you in the abode of Majesty.'

When the time of Asr comes and they rise, perform ablution, and pray, he brings for them from God, mighty and majestic, the third writ, written therein: 'I am God, the Majestic. Majestic is My remembrance and great is My dominion. My servants and handmaids, I have forbidden your bodies from the Fire, and I have settled you in the dwellings of the righteous, and I have repelled from you by My mercy the evil of the wicked.'

When the time of Maghrib comes and they rise, perform ablution, and pray, he brings for them from God, mighty and majestic, the fourth writ, written therein: 'I am God, the Compeller, the Grand, the Most High. My servants and handmaids, My angels have ascended from you with satisfaction, and it is due upon Me to please you and give you on the Day of Resurrection your wishes.'

When the time of Isha comes and they rise, perform ablution, and pray, he brings for them from God, mighty and majestic, the fifth writ, written therein: 'Indeed I am God. There is no deity other than Me, and no lord besides Me. My servants and handmaids, in your homes you purified yourselves, and to My houses you walked, and in My remembrance you immersed yourselves, and My right you recognized, and My obligations you fulfilled. I call you to witness, O Sakha'il, and the rest of My angels, that I am indeed pleased with them.'

He said: Then Sakha'il calls with three calls every night after the Isha prayer: 'O angels of God! Indeed God, blessed and exalted, has forgiven the praying monotheists.' Then no angel remains in the seven heavens except that he seeks forgiveness for those who pray and supplicates for them to persevere in that. Whoever is granted the night prayer, whether male servant or female servant, who stands for God, mighty and majestic, sincerely, performs a thorough ablution, and prays for God, mighty and majestic, with truthful intention, a sound heart, a humble body, and tearful eyes - God, blessed and exalted, places behind him nine rows of angels, in each row a number that none can count except God, blessed and exalted, one end of each row in the East and the other in the West.

He said: When he finishes, there are written for him ranks equal to their number. Mansur said: al-Rabi' ibn Badr, whenever he narrated this hadith, would say: 'Where are you, O heedless one, from this generosity? And where are you from standing in this night? And from the abundance of this reward, and from this honour?'
ai.seo_question: What does Islam teach about the rewards of the five daily prayers and the night prayer?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition describes an angel named Sakha'il who brings five divine writs of forgiveness for those who perform the five daily prayers, each bearing a unique Divine Name and promise, plus the extraordinary reward of the night prayer with nine rows of uncountable angels.
